## Grading

We will grade your **code before the poster session**, and a **poster presentation**, consisting of a **poster walkthrough** (4min) and ~10 minutes of **questions / answers**.

### Code - 35% (graded before the poster session)

- **10% Code readability & code documentation.** Same as before: direct documentation (code comments), docstrings, style and modularity. One difference to the report-based version: since there is no methods section anymore, the *why* behind your choices (reference, filter settings, data removal criteria, algorithmic choices) should appear in short comments where the choice is made. I do not want essays in the code — one or two sharp sentences per decision ("average reference, because ...") 

- **10% Reproducibility & modularity.** Control and document the software versions, make sure your analysis scripts can be reproduced on another computer easily. If you are using mne-BIDS-pipeline you already have a good start

- **15% Sanity checks & sanity visualizations.** Small asserts & plots here and there, maybe even a unittest or two- small things that make sure your code is doing what it is supposed to be doing.

### Poster - 15%

Poster should consist of:
- pipeline overview with own choices 
- Results (including results of original-authors to compare with). 
- Results of additional analyses

### Walkthrough - 20% (4 min sharp)

You walk us through your poster, present your pipelines, your motivation for change, your results (whether you think you replicated or not) and your additional analysis.

### Q&A - 30% (~10 min)

We will mainly ask for motivation of selected parameters: why this reference, why these filters, why did you remove these epochs, why this algorithm etc. Sometimes there is no correct answer, so I want to hear what your thoughts were choosing either or. "The pipeline did it" is not a good answer, but "we changed X and it did Y" would be. We will not quiz you on specific knowledge of EEG (we won't ask e.g. "how does ICA relate to PCA")
